text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's Krajowa Partia Emerytow i Rencistow (KPEiR) pensioners' party has created 26 election committees and others are being formed. The party will run alone in the parliamentary elections. Preserving stable economic growth is the party's priority as this will improve living conditions of pensioners, the jobless, homeless, and one-parent families, KPEiR said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Italian representatives to the EU have protested against a planned increase in the minimum number of parts to be used in vehicle assembly by Korea's Daewoo plants in Poland, for fear that the same rules will be imposed on other car makers including Italy's Fiat. The matter will go for arbitrage to the World Customs Organisation.

- The state-owned CPN petrol distribution chain will pass 100 percent of shares in the DEC petrol tanks transport unit to the Naftobaza company, to be registered by the end of the month. Naftobaza is a subsidiary of the Nafta Polska holding.
- The listed Mostostal Zabrze construction firm has started work at the future Opel plant's site in Gliwice, southern Poland. The contract is worth $87.6 million.

- Fiat Auto Poland's shareholders have decided to pass 84 million zlotys from the 311 million net profit earned in 1996 to cover losses made the year before. The remaining 277 million zlotys will fuel inventory capital and reserve capital.
- Daewoo will start assemblying Nexia cars in its Lublin plant with the use of car parts made in Romania, Daewoo Motor Polska official Zbigniew Pazdzior said.

- The Polish corporate sector's sales in January and Febuary this year reached 95.2 billion zlotys out of which 48.1 billion zlotys accounted for the private sector's sales, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said. The companies' gross profit totalled 3.8 billion zlotys in the period.

- Turkey's Rumeli cement concern, which holds a 75 percent stake in the Nowa Huta cement mill, has discharged the plant's president Alojzy Malczak and deputy president Leszek Myrdka. Bunyamin Eroglu was appointed Nowa Huta's new president.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- Securities houses operating on a strong capital base will increase their market share in the years to come at the cost of small brokerages, HSBC Investment Banking/HSBC Investment Services President Hubert Janiszewski said.

- Merrill Lynch investment bank changed its rating of Poland's capital markets to neutral as a result of the nearing parliamentary elections, which may result in forming a government less favourable to market reforms than the present cabinet.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati has discussed Poland's access to the Asian Development Bank (ADB) with the Philippines' Foreign Minister Domingo Siazon during his current vist to Manila. The Philippines will support Poland's possible membership application, Siazon said.
ZYCIE

- Germany's Praktiker supermarket chain will open its first construction material supermarket in Janki, at the outskirts of Warsaw, this month. The chain plans to open 40 supermarkets around the country in the next seven years.
PARKIET

- Mostostal Siedlce construction firm will present a share issue prospectus to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) by the end of May, the firm said. Following the issue's registration Mostostal's share capital will be 7.4 million zlotys.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
